agreement: Two agreements, plus a third settlement contract. (1) A 'Grant Agreement' with Defendant as 'Grantee' under which JobsOhio agreed to provide $130,000.00 in grant funds. (2) A 'Talent Acquisition Services Agreement' ('TAS Agreement'), which the attached demand letter prices at $273,000, under which JobsOhio agreed to provide services rather than cash: 'assisting in selecting and enhancing Defendant's overall candidate attraction strategies related to pre-selected job postings and media channels, seeking to increase the volume of candidates applying to open positions at the company through a variety of job posting and advertising strategies, increasing community awareness of Defendant and its role as an employer in the local area, and providing website design, and data services.' Complaint para. 6: 'The TAS Agreement provided that JobsOhio would utilize subcontractors in performance of the talent acquisition services, with JobsOhio agreeing to fund such services up to a specified amount, and Defendant agreeing to repay JobsOhio the cost of such services should Defendant fail to create a specified number of new jobs, to retain a specified number of existing jobs, and to maintain specified payroll levels for each at the Project Site.' (3) A 'Payment Plan Agreement' formed by email in October 2025.
agreement_date: Grant Agreement 'on or about April 24, 2020'; TAS Agreement 'on or about September 28, 2021'; Payment Plan Agreement reached October 2025, first payment due November 1, 2025
program: Not named. The complaint never names any of JobsOhio's 12 published programs. It describes JobsOhio's method only as 'providing incentives to companies conditioned on their meeting specified, as applicable, fixed asset investment, job creation, job retention, job training, and payroll and training cost commitments pursuant to one or more formal written agreements.'
amount_sought: $204,750.83, plus interest including prejudgment interest, costs, expenses, reasonable attorney fees. This is the balance after crediting the one payment made under the Payment Plan Agreement. The underlying admitted liability was $216,795.00, being $130,000.00 on the Grant Agreement (the full grant) and $86,795.00 on the TAS Agreement.
job_commitments: Grant Agreement, per Exhibit 1 (demand letter of 2025-08-14) citing Section 5: creation of 64 jobs with associated payroll of $2,169,856, retention of 535 jobs with associated payroll of $22,945,897, and $2,000,000 in Fixed Asset Investments. Metric Evaluation Date December 31, 2022; Metric Expiration Date December 31, 2024. TAS Agreement, per Exhibit 2 citing Section 2: create 82 jobs with associated payroll of $2,797,184, retain 618 jobs with associated payroll of $25,305,783, and create $1,702,500 in fixed asset investment. Metric Evaluation Date December 31, 2023; Metric Expiration Date December 31, 2025. Project Site for both: 250 Eastern Avenue, Leesburg, Ohio 45135.
shortfall: Grant Agreement, per the company's 2024 Annual Report as quoted in Exhibit 1: 'created 0 new jobs with an associated payroll of $0.00, and that it had retained 346 jobs with an associated payroll of $17,049,586. Additionally, Grantee reported $650,000.00 in Fixed Asset Investments.' TAS Agreement, per the company's 2023 Annual Report as quoted in Exhibit 2: 'created only 0 new jobs with an associated payroll of $0. Additionally, Candle-lite Company, LLC reported that it had retained only 428 jobs with an associated payroll of $23,617,642.'
remedy_named: Liquidated damages, for the TAS Agreement. Exhibit 2, the TAS demand letter of 2025-08-14: 'Therefore, pursuant to Section 9(a) of the Agreement, Company is in Breach of the Agreement. As a result of this Breach, and pursuant to Section 9(b)(ii) of the Agreement, JobsOhio demands that Company pay to JobsOhio as liquidated damages the service value performed under the Agreement in the amount of $86,795.00. The amount demanded to be repaid takes into account the number of jobs and payroll Company created, the total fixed assets invested in the Project, as well as the Market Conditions and Other Factors provided by Company to JobsOhio.' For the Grant Agreement, Exhibit 1 uses the same section numbers but the word repay rather than liquidated damages: 'Therefore, pursuant to Section 9(a) of the Agreement, Grantee is in Breach of the Agreement. As a result of this Breach, and pursuant to Section 9(b)(ii) of the Agreement, JobsOhio demands that Grantee repay to JobsOhio the Grant Funds disbursed under the Agreement, in the amount of $130,000.' The complaint itself paraphrases: 'Defendant agreed that in the event of a breach, JobsOhio could recover up to the entire amount of its grant.'
agreement_is_exhibit: No, neither agreement. Complaint para. 4: 'A copy of the Grant Agreement is not attached hereto as Defendant already has a copy in its possession.' Complaint para. 5: 'A copy of the TAS Agreement is not attached hereto as Defendant already has a copy in its possession, and as it contains confidential and trade secret information.' The three exhibits are the two demand letters of 2025-08-14 and the October 2025 email thread setting the payment plan.
outcome: Default judgment for JobsOhio. Motion for default judgment filed 2026-08-20, granted 2026-09-09. 'JUDGMENT ENTRY GRANTING PLAINTIFF JOBSOHIO JUDGMENT AGAINST DEFENDANT CANDLE-LITE COMPANY, LLC ... ORDERED that JobsOhio is granted judgment against Defendant Candle-Lite Company, LLC in the amount of $192,706.83, plus costs and statutory interest from the date of this Judgment.' Signed Judge Jeffrey M. Brown. Case terminated 2026-09-09. No attorney ever appeared for the defendant. No satisfaction of judgment appears on the docket; instead JobsOhio filed a praecipe requesting a certificate of judgment on 2026-09-24 and the certificate was sent to its counsel on 2026-09-30, which is a collection step.
amount_recovered: Not stated in any filing. The judgment is $192,706.83, which is $12,044.17 less than the $204,750.83 sought, and the docket shows no satisfaction of judgment as of 2026-11-03. One payment of $12,044.17 was made under the Payment Plan Agreement before suit.

notes: The complaint does NOT block-quote the agreements. It paraphrases them, so repayment_quote is empty. The verbatim section language in this case comes from the two JobsOhio demand letters attached as Exhibits 1 and 2 and signed by Don Grubbs, General Counsel. Those letters cite Section 5 (Grant Agreement metric commitments), Section 2 (TAS Agreement metric commitments), Section 9(a) (Breach) and Section 9(b)(ii) (remedy) but do not reproduce the sections word for word. Two findings worth carrying: the same company held both a cash grant agreement and a Talent Acquisition Services Agreement, and the TAS remedy is styled liquidated damages measured by 'the service value performed under the Agreement,' matching the structure seen in the Olive AI case. Exhibit 3 is an email thread in which the company's general manager writes 'we definitely appreciate the 18-month extension' but asks for a one-month deferral; the company then made a single $12,044.17 payment of the 18 scheduled.

defendant: REPUBLIC STEEL (a Delaware corporation registered in Ohio; project site 1807 East 28th Street, Lorain, OH 44055-1803)
agreement: 'Grant Agreement' with Defendant as the Grantee, plus an 'Amendment to Grant Agreement'. The agreement itself is headed 'JOBSOHIO GRANT AGREEMENT' and bears 'Program No.: SFPN_2018_458489-WF'. JobsOhio agreed to provide 'up to $500,000.00 in grant funds, on a reimbursement basis.' The agreement's own recital: 'Grantee will use the financial assistance in accordance with JobsOhio's grant guidelines to invest in workforce training associated with Grantee's project at the Project Address identified above (the "Project").' Grant Funds line on page 1: $500,000. Effective Date on the agreement's own first page is September 4, 2018, while the complaint pleads the parties entered into it on February 20, 2019.
agreement_date: Complaint para. 4: 'On February 20, 2019, JobsOhio entered into a Grant Agreement with Defendant as the Grantee.' The agreement's own cover page gives an Effective Date of September 4, 2018. Amendment to Grant Agreement dated August 5, 2021.
program: Not named in words, but the attached agreement carries 'Program No.: SFPN_2018_458489-WF' and its recital points to 'JobsOhio's grant guidelines to invest in workforce training.' The complaint itself never names one of JobsOhio's 12 published programs; it says only that JobsOhio works 'through the use of strategic grants and project funding.'
amount_sought: $300,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees, costs and expenses. This is the amount actually disbursed, not the $500,000 the agreement authorized. The complaint pleads JobsOhio 'provided Defendant $300,000.00 in grant funds.'
job_commitments: From the agreement's own first page, Metric Commitments: Total Fixed Asset Investment $890,000; No. of Jobs to be Created 125; No. of Employees to be Trained 85; Total Payroll to be Created $7,000,000; Total Training Investment $1,804,550. Metric Evaluation Date December 31, 2021, amended to December 31, 2022. Metric Expiration Date December 31, 2023, amended to December 31, 2024. Project Site 1807 East 28th Street, Lorain, OH.
shortfall: Complaint para. 9: 'pursuant to Defendant's 2022 Annual Report, Defendant only created 55 new jobs at the Project Site instead of the required 125 new jobs, and the new jobs had an associated payroll of $3,106,666.00, instead of the required $7,000,000.00.'
repayment_quote: Section 5, as block-quoted at complaint para. 5: '5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under section 9 of this Agreement. *** (Emphasis added).' || Section 6(b), as block-quoted at complaint para. 6: '(b) Annual Reports. Grantee shall submit to Grantor an annual report in the format required by Grantor (the "Annual Report"). Each Annual Report shall provide information for the applicable reporting period detailing the progress of the Project, and Metric Commitments to date. Annual Reports shall be submitted by Grantee for each calendar year (or part of a year) during the Term of this Agreement, and each Annual Report shall be received by Grantor no later than March 1 following the calendar year covered by such Annual Report. Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9. (Emphasis added).' || Section 9(a) and 9(b), as block-quoted at complaint para. 7: '(a) Breach. Grantee shall be deemed to be in "Breach" of this Agreement if: *** (ii) Grantee fails to comply with the Metric Commitment requirements set forth in Section 5 hereof; (iii) Grantee fails to timely comply with its reporting obligations under Section 6 hereof; (iv) Grantee fails to maintain substantial operations at the Project Address during the Term. *** (b) Effect of Breach; Remedies. In the event of a Breach by Grantor, Grantee may pursue any legal or equitable remedies it may have under this Agreement or applicable law. In the event of a Breach by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (Emphasis added). (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law.' || Section 9(e), quoted in part at complaint para. 12: Defendant is liable for JobsOhio's 'expenses, including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees, in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement.' || The full Grant Agreement is also attached as Exhibit 1, so its Section 9 appears in full on the record, including language not quoted in the complaint body: '9. Default and Remedies. Except to the extent that this Agreement or applicable law requires otherwise, the remedies set forth in this Section are the sole and exclusive remedies available upon a violation, default or Breach of this Agreement.' and, in Section 5(c): 'Notwithstanding, Grantor has the discretion to waive non-compliance if, in writing, Grantee submits to Grantor a description of Market Conditions and Other Factors regarding Grantee and its operations at the Project site. Grantor will review and consider such Market Conditions and Other Factors submitted and may waive repayment of all or a portion of the Grant Funds disbursed.' and, in Section 5: 'For the purpose of this Agreement, "jobs" - both retained and created - are calculated on a full time equivalent (FTE) annual basis, obtained by dividing the total number of hours for which employees were compensated for employment in the Project by two-thousand eighty.'
remedy_named: Repayment. The remedy heading is 'Demand Repayment of Grant Funds' at Section 9(b)(ii), inside Section 9 'Default and Remedies.' It is not called a clawback and it is not called liquidated damages. Section 9 states these are 'the sole and exclusive remedies.' Section 5(c) gives JobsOhio discretion to waive repayment on a written showing of 'Market Conditions and Other Factors.'
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. This is the exception. Complaint para. 4: 'JobsOhio entered into a Grant Agreement with Defendant as the Grantee, a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit 1.' The Amendment to Grant Agreement is Exhibit 2 and the demand letter of July 27, 2023 is Exhibit 3. The full text of the JobsOhio form Grant Agreement, including Sections 1 through 10 and the Metric Commitments table, is therefore on the public record in this case.
outcome: Dismissed by JobsOhio with prejudice. Republic Steel appeared through Tucker Ellis LLP and Nelson Mullins and filed an Answer on 2023-12-15. On 2024-03-13 JobsOhio filed a 'NOTICE OF VOLUNTARY DISMISSAL WITH PREJUDICE': 'Pursuant to Civ.R. 41(A)(1)(a), Plaintiff JobsOhio hereby dismisses all claims against Defendant Republic Steel with prejudice. Each party will bear their own costs and attorneys' fees.' Case terminated the same day. No judgment was ever entered.
amount_recovered: Not stated in any filing. No judgment was entered and no settlement terms appear on the docket. The dismissal says only that each party bears its own costs and fees. The record does not establish that JobsOhio recovered anything.

notes: The single most useful case in this batch. It is the one complaint that both block-quotes the agreement and attaches the whole agreement as an exhibit, so the JobsOhio form Grant Agreement text is public here. Three things stand out. First, the remedy for missing job commitments is a plain repayment demand under Section 9(b)(ii), payable within 30 days, not a clawback formula and not liquidated damages. Second, Section 9 says the listed remedies 'are the sole and exclusive remedies.' Third, Section 5(c) lets JobsOhio waive repayment entirely at its own discretion if the company writes in describing 'Market Conditions and Other Factors,' which Section 5(d) defines broadly enough to include 'an overall decline in economic performance' and 'Grantee's overall presence in the State of Ohio.' Republic Steel is also the only defendant in this batch that hired counsel and answered, and the suit for $300,000 was then dismissed with prejudice four months later with each side bearing its own fees. The $500,000 on the Form 990 schedule does not match the $300,000 pleaded as disbursed under this agreement, and the court record does not reconcile the two.
